answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a scarce, non-transferable reputation credential by completing small jobs that established peers verify and stake collateral on. A whisper from a trusted reviewer may flag suspicious work, but one reviewer cannot mint credentials alone; multiple independent attestations and a challenge period are required. An attacker who tries to forge many identities must fund each credential, recruit or fool verifiers, and keep those identities useful long enough to recover the cost. Even a cedar-themed name gains no weight by itself.
